# AgentCanvas

> A friendlier way to steer the app an AI is building for you. AgentCanvas keeps repo evidence and the display canvas separate, so an AI coding agent can turn code behavior into plain-English flows and only implement source changes when asked.

## What it is

AgentCanvas is a local, agent-agnostic tool. It indexes a workspace into `.agentcanvas/workflow.ir.json`, then the invoking agent turns that evidence into simple **journeys** stored in `.agentcanvas/canvas.ir.json`: **When / Do / If** steps with if/else branches. Use `agentcanvas canvas apply` to update that canvas so validation, revision checks, and automatic legacy migration run before the browser reads it. A person can edit a step ("add a step", "change what happens", "add a rule", "remove a step") in their own words. Canvas-only edits update the display canvas, not source code.

## Who it's for

Non-technical people (operators, founders, power users) who want to understand and steer an app an AI agent is building, without reading code.

## How an AI coding agent uses it

1. Start it: `agentcanvas up .` (install: `pip install use-agentcanvas`). It serves a local web canvas and prints a URL.
2. Read `.agentcanvas/workflow.ir.json` as raw evidence and write/update the browser canvas with `agentcanvas canvas apply`.
3. For canvas edits, keep applying operation batches through `agentcanvas canvas apply`. Do not re-index unless evidence needs to be refreshed.
4. For explicit source-code implementation requests, read `.agentcanvas/pending/`, implement the change in code, run the relevant tests, re-index with `agentcanvas index --workspace .` to refresh evidence, and report what changed.

Any AI coding agent that can read files and run commands can use it. Copy-paste fallback is always available.

## Key facts

- Local-first, runs from the command line.
- Agent-agnostic (no vendor lock-in).
- `.agentcanvas/workflow.ir.json` is the raw index/evidence file.
- `.agentcanvas/canvas.ir.json` is the stored browser canvas; update it through `agentcanvas canvas apply`.
- Legacy display canvases auto-migrate the first time `agentcanvas canvas apply` edits them.
- Canvas edits are canvas changes, not direct code changes, unless the user explicitly asks for implementation.
